title: Batcher queue livelock: short-term mitigations and long-term mitigation plan
creator: Raj Patel
description: Summary: During a Friday evening capacity surge we observed repeated batcher queue livelock where worker shards accepted requests but made no forward progress for 20-90s intervals, causing token-level tail latency spikes and request retries. This ticket captures the incident follow-up, immediate mitigations we applied, root cause analysis, and a prioritized set of action items (short-term fixes and long-term systemic changes).
timeline: 2026-02-27 18:12 UTC: Alert — per-route p99 token latency > 10s on inference-west-1 (alerts/runtime/p99-token-latency).
2026-02-27 18:18 UTC: On-call rotated; initial mitigation scaled up dedicated pool by 2x which reduced new request enqueueing but didn’t fully resolve tail spikes.
2026-02-27 18:30 UTC: Observed repeated batches with size > 256 but zero token emission for 30-60s. Affected models: gpt-neoX-20B-quant and rwd-compat-13B.
2026-02-27 18:45 UTC: Investigations showed batch formation threads entered a tight loop waiting on a per-shard queue condition while KV cache evictions raced with request pinning.

2026-02-27 18:55 UTC: Applied short-term mitigation: reduced max batch size, tightened batch-formation timeout to 150ms, and disabled cross-shard speculative merging. Token emission resumed and p99 improved but remained elevated under load.
2026-02-27 20:10 UTC: Traffic restored to normal shape; on-call declared incident mitigated. Post-incident timeline collection initiated.
2026-03-01: Postmortem kickoff and initial RCA draft completed.
root_cause_summary: The livelock was caused by a race between the batch formation scheduler and the KV cache reclamation path under heavy concurrent evictions. When eviction latency spiked (due to increased cache thrashing on large-context requests), batcher worker threads repeatedly requeued requests while attempting to pin KV shards, hitting a path that rechecked queue emptiness without yielding. This produced tight CPU loops on some shards and starvation on others (fairness inversion), preventing token emission for affected batches even though requests were accepted.
mitigation_applied: Reduced max_batch_size from 512 to 192 for affected model families (runtime-1.21 override).
Lowered batch-formation max_wait from 500ms to 150ms and made timeout jittered to avoid synchronized wakeups.
Disabled cross-shard speculative merge for the hot route for 6 hours while we stabilized cache behavior.
Scaled dedicated pool capacity by 2x during peak and enabled immediate throttling for non-critical background evaluation jobs.
Added emergency dashboard widget surfacing batcher spinning CPU per-shard and KV eviction latency (grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/Batcher/queue-livelock).
impact_metrics: Peak affected requests: ~11k requests/min across 3 host shards.
Median additional end-to-end latency during incident: +320ms.
P99 token latency before mitigation: 12s; after short-term mitigations: 1.8s.
Customer-visible retries increased by ~7% for the 2h window.
No customer data loss; requests were retried or completed once token emission resumed.
long_term_root_cause_notes: Batch formation code assumes quick KV pin/unpin operations; under heavy eviction pressure these operations may block or suffer priority inversions.
Scheduler wakeups were synchronized across shards leading to periodic coordinated stalls (lockstep requeues).
No explicit backoff/yield path existed in the hot loop used when a shard cannot progress due to external resources (KV cache).
Telemetry lacked per-batch state indicating 'pinned-but-no-progress' which hindered automated detection and routing to fallback model variants.
action_items: Short-term: Implement yield-based backoff in batcher hot loop and add an exponential backoff up to 1s. Owner: June Park. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-20.
Short-term: Add metric 'batcher_shard_spin_seconds' and alert if >5s for any shard. Owner: Marcus Liu. Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-10 (DONE).
Medium-term: Introduce per-batch 'progress' heartbeat and circuit-breaker to abort and reroute batches stuck >2s to a lower-latency model variant. Owner: Sanya Iyer. Estimate: 8. Due: 2026-04-15.
Medium-term: Improve KV cache eviction path to avoid long stop-the-world pauses; implement incremental eviction with cooperative yielding. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Estimate: 13. Due: 2026-05-01.
Long-term: Rework scheduler to use randomized staggered wakeups and per-shard token-buckets to prevent synchronized requeues. Owner: Runtime Platform. Estimate: 20. Due: 2026-06-01.
Long-term: Add chaos tests in CI that simulate heavy cache thrashing + high concurrency to validate livelock regressions. Owner: Reliability QA. Estimate: 8. Due: 2026-05-20.
Operational: Draft runbook for batcher livelock incidents with clear playbook (scale, timeout overrides, disable speculative features). Owner: Oncall Eng. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-14.
Policy: Add release gate for batcher hot-loop changes to require performance bench and staging chaos test results. Owner: Eng Manager Runtime. Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-31.
prioritization_rationale: We prioritize fixes that reduce customer-visible tail latency with smallest blast radius first: observability and backoffs (low-risk) -> per-batch circuit-breaker and KV eviction improvements (higher effort) -> scheduler rework (largest scope).
postdeployment_validation: Canary rollout of backoff change to 10% of shards for 24 hours with synthetic high-concurrency workload; verify p99 token latency improvement and no throughput regression.
Run k8s job to reproduce cache-thrashing scenario from incident and validate cooperative eviction prevents >2s stalls.
Monitor 'batcher_shard_spin_seconds' and 'per-batch progress' metric; require zero spikes in 48h before wider rollout.
